Getting started with easyNIS

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

easyNIS takes you from annual National Inpatient Sample (NIS) Parquet files to a survey-weighted table, with primary small cells suppressed. This guide walks through the steps on nis_example() data: invented discharges that have the NIS column layout but no real records. Replace the example path with the directory that holds your own NIS_<year>.parquet files to run a real study.

Open the data

nis_open() opens the annual files lazily, so nothing is read into memory until you ask for it. Mixed-case NIS column names are normalized across years; wholly lower-case names are left unchanged.

path <- nis_example(years = 2019:2020)
nis <- nis_open(path)

nis |>
  dplyr::count(YEAR) |>
  dplyr::collect()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>    YEAR     n
#>   <int> <int>
#> 1  2019    96
#> 2  2020    96

Flag diagnoses and procedures

nis_flag_dx() and nis_flag_pr() add one logical column per named set of ICD-10 code prefixes. Each diagnosis or procedure slot is checked on its own, and the work stays lazy. Prefixes ignore case, periods, and spaces; stored codes must use the NIS upper-case, period-free layout.

nis <- nis |>
  nis_flag_dx(
    heart_failure = "I50",
    palliative_care = "Z515"
  ) |>
  nis_flag_pr(ablation = "02L")

nis |>
  dplyr::count(heart_failure, palliative_care) |>
  dplyr::collect()
#> # A tibble: 4 × 3
#>   heart_failure palliative_care     n
#>   <lgl>         <lgl>           <int>
#> 1 TRUE          FALSE              88
#> 2 FALSE         FALSE              66
#> 3 TRUE          TRUE               20
#> 4 FALSE         TRUE               18

Use position = "principal" to look at the principal diagnosis only. To build the prefix lists from an HCUP CCSR reference file that you download yourself, see nis_ccsr_codes().

Build the survey design

nis_design() takes a cohort expression and the columns to keep, collects the cohort, and returns a nested survey design. It adds a placeholder row for each hospital-year with no cohort discharges, so variance estimates account for the whole sample. It also labels coded fields, and, when TOTCHG and CCR_NIS are kept, adds inflation-adjusted cost_adj and charges_adj.

design <- nis_design(
  nis,
  cohort = heart_failure & AGE >= 18,
  keep = c(AGE, FEMALE, DIED, LOS, TOTCHG, CCR_NIS, palliative_care),
  dollars = 2024
)
#> Cohort: 108 discharges; weighted N 124.8; 18 hospitals across 2 years.

Discharges with a missing or invalid design field are excluded with a warning that gives their number. The design-based tools in the survey and srvyr packages work on the result as they would on any other design.

srvyr::summarise(
  design,
  discharges = srvyr::survey_total(),
  mean_los = srvyr::survey_mean(LOS)
)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   discharges discharges_se mean_los mean_los_se
#>        <dbl>         <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1       125.          17.3     5.66       0.229

Table 1 and a model

gtsummary::tbl_svysummary() builds a weighted table from the design, and survey::svyglm() fits a model that uses the survey structure.

The table chunks need the optional gtsummary, cardx, survey, and gt packages. Install them before running this guide if they are not already available.

table_one <- gtsummary::tbl_svysummary(
  design,
  by = palliative_care,
  include = c(AGE, FEMALE, LOS, cost_adj)
) |>
  gtsummary::add_overall()
fit <- survey::svyglm(
  LOS ~ palliative_care + AGE + FEMALE + factor(YEAR),
  design = design
)

summary(fit)
#> 
#> Call:
#> svyglm(formula = LOS ~ palliative_care + AGE + FEMALE + factor(YEAR), 
#>     design = design)
#> 
#> Survey design:
#> Called via srvyr
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>                      Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
#> (Intercept)         6.132e+00  6.441e-01   9.520 1.22e-05 ***
#> palliative_careYes  1.679e+00  9.073e-01   1.850   0.1014    
#> AGE                -5.156e-03  1.310e-02  -0.394   0.7041    
#> FEMALEFemale       -9.736e-01  3.230e-01  -3.014   0.0167 *  
#> factor(YEAR)2020   -7.866e-16  4.318e-01   0.000   1.0000    
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#> 
#> (Dispersion parameter for gaussian family taken to be 11.32638)
#> 
#> Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 2

Suppress small cells

HCUP data use agreements require suppressing cells that describe 10 or fewer discharges. nis_suppress() masks displayed statistics whose unweighted count is at or below the threshold, along with the overall cell in the same row, and adds a footnote that says so. Review tables for other derivable cells, such as column totals, before you share them.

nis_suppress(table_one, threshold = 10)
Characteristic Overall
N = 1251,2 		No
N = 1011,2 		Yes
N = 231,2
Age, years 59 (41, 76) 59 (38, 73) 64 (49, 79)
Sex of patient


    Male Masked 51 (50%) ≤10
    Female Masked 50 (50%) ≤10
Length of stay, days 6.0 (3.0, 9.0) 6.0 (2.0, 8.0) 10.0 (3.0, 10.0)
Hospital cost (2024 USD) 5,405 (5,257, 5,557) 5,396 (5,253, 5,557) 5,407 (5,272, 5,540)
1 Median (Q1, Q3); n (%)
2 Statistics based on unweighted n ≤10 are marked ≤10. Overall cells in rows with a masked by-group cell are marked 'Masked' unless their own count is at or below the threshold. Other derivable cells are not masked; review tables for other derivable cells before sharing under the HCUP Data Use Agreement.

Start a study folder

nis_new_study() copies a Quarto template to a new directory. The template reproduces the steps above as a report with cohort flow, Table 1, outcomes, yearly trends, and regression tables. Its analysis.qmd runs on invented data until you set its data_path parameter.

study <- tempfile("my-nis-study-")
nis_new_study(study)
#> [1] "/tmp/Rtmp0nQC09/my-nis-study-1cf21c9334aa"
list.files(study, all.files = TRUE, no.. = TRUE)
#> [1] "_quarto.yml"  ".gitignore"   "analysis.qmd"

Edit the definitions block in analysis.qmd for your cohort, then render it with Quarto.

Where next

The “Porting an existing NIS study to easyNIS” vignette maps common regular-expression and recoding steps to easyNIS. nis_reweight() applies propensity weights to a design, and nis_comorbidity() adds AHRQ Elixhauser columns; both are experimental.
